title: Logo draws then fills
sub: Outline traces itself, fill floods in

<g class="mark" transform="translate(100 22)">

  <path class="out" d="M50 18Q60 8 70 18L102 50Q112 60 102 70L70 102Q60 112 50 102L18 70Q8 60 18 50Z"/>
  <path class="core" d="M60 33Q62 58 87 60Q62 62 60 87Q58 62 33 60Q58 58 60 33Z" fill="#fff" stroke="none"/>

prompt: Build a logo reveal for a hero or splash screen using GSAP 3 with DrawSVGPlugin. Draw the mark as inline SVG: a rounded diamond outline path, a four point star path inside it, and a duplicate of the diamond filled with a blue gradient. Use stroke-linecap and stroke-linejoin round, stroke-width 3. Register the plugin with gsap.registerPlugin(DrawSVGPlugin), then in one timeline: gsap.fromTo(outline, { drawSVG: '0%' }, { drawSVG: '100%', duration: 1.2, ease: 'power2.inOut' }), start the star stroke 0.45s later, fade the fill in at about 1.35s with opacity 0 to 1, then retract the outline with drawSVG: '100% 100%' so the stroke runs off the end of the path while the fill takes over. Finally rise the wordmark and tagline in with y 10 to 0, power3.out, stagger 0.1. Wrap it in gsap.context(() => {...}, svgElement) and call ctx.revert() on unmount. A round cap draws a dot at zero length, so keep late strokes at opacity 0 until their start. Under prefers-reduced-motion show the finished logo with no tween. Colours: your accent color for stroke and fill, near-black ink for the wordmark.

prompt: Build an icon button whose glyph morphs between four states (menu, close, arrow, check) with GSAP 3 MorphSVGPlugin. Draw each glyph in a 24 unit viewBox with stroke 2, round caps and joins, and give all four shapes the same number of sub paths so every stroke has a partner: menu 'M4 6H20M4 12H20M4 18H20', close 'M6 6L18 18M6 18L18 6M6 18L18 6', arrow 'M4 12H20M14 6L20 12M14 18L20 12', check 'M4 13L9 18M9 18L20 7M9 18L20 7' (the duplicated last stroke avoids a stray point). Register MorphSVGPlugin, then step with gsap.to(path, { morphSVG: { shape: nextD, shapeIndex: 0 }, duration: 1, ease: 'elastic.out(1, 0.7)' }) so each state overshoots and settles like a spring. Pulse the button scale 0.9 to 1 with elastic.out(1, 0.5) on every step and swap the label with a short y shift and fade. On a real site drive it from a click handler with a single paused timeline per transition, keep the button a real <button> with aria-label updated per state, and under prefers-reduced-motion set the d attribute directly with no tween.

prompt: Build a delivery route animation with GSAP 3 using DrawSVGPlugin and MotionPathPlugin. Author one SVG path for the route (two smooth cubic curves), keep an invisible copy as the motion guide, and layer a dashed copy of it (stroke-dasharray '1 8.5', round caps) clipped by an SVG mask whose white stroked path is the one you animate, plus a solid accent copy for the travelled trail. Register both plugins. In one timeline run three tweens from time 0: the mask path with drawSVG '0% 0%' to '0% 100%' (2.4s, power2.out) so the route reveals ahead of the vehicle, the trail with the same drawSVG over 3.4s power1.inOut, and the vehicle with gsap.to(car, { motionPath: { path: routeEl, align: routeEl, alignOrigin: [0.5, 0.5], autoRotate: true }, duration: 3.4, ease: 'power1.inOut' }). Draw the car pointing along +x so autoRotate faces it forward. On arrival bounce the destination pin (scale 1.2 then elastic.out(1, 0.5)) and fade an ETA chip up. Wrap in gsap.context and revert on unmount; with prefers-reduced-motion jump the timeline to its end.

Register the plugins and build one timeline: for each stroke, read stroke.getTotalLength() and set duration = 0.3 + length / 170 so long strokes take longer, tween gsap.fromTo(stroke, { drawSVG: '0%' }, { drawSVG: '100%', ease }) using sine.inOut for the cursive strokes and power2.out for the swoosh, and leave a 0.14s pause between strokes like a lifted pen. Keep each stroke at opacity 0 until its start because a round cap draws a dot at zero length. Move a small pen nib dot along the same path with motionPath: { path: stroke, align: stroke, alignOrigin: [0.5, 0.5] } on the same duration and ease, hiding it between strokes. When the last stroke lands, fade in a "Signed by" caption and a pill. Use gsap.context and revert on unmount; with prefers-reduced-motion render the finished signature.

prompt: Build a morphing blob hero backdrop with GSAP 3 MorphSVGPlugin. Author four organic blob paths that each use exactly eight anchor points sampled around the same centre starting at the same angle, with a different radius per anchor, converted to smooth closed cubic curves. Same point count and start angle means MorphSVG interpolates point to point and the shape wobbles instead of twisting inside out. Put two blobs behind the headline: a large pale one and a smaller one filled with a soft blue gradient at partial opacity. Register the plugin and loop a repeating timeline: gsap.to(blob, { morphSVG: { shape: nextD, type: 'linear' }, duration: 2, ease: 'sine.inOut' }) stepping A to B to C to D and back to A, with the back blob running the same sequence offset by two shapes and 0.15s later. Keep headline text in front, at least 4.5:1 against the lightest part of the blob. Use gsap.context and revert on unmount; with prefers-reduced-motion show one static shape.

prompt: Build a success confirmation animation with GSAP 3 and DrawSVGPlugin for a payment or form screen. In one SVG: a pale accent disc, a ring path drawn as two arcs starting at 12 o'clock (so drawSVG runs clockwise from the top), a check path 'M138 102L154 118L184 84' with stroke-width 7 and round caps, an outline circle for a pulse and twelve short radial tick lines. Register DrawSVGPlugin and sequence one timeline: pop the disc (scale 0.6 to 1, back.out(1.6)), draw the ring 0% to 100% over 0.8s power2.inOut, stroke the check in over 0.45s power3.out, then launch the pulse ring (scale 1 to 1.7, opacity 0.9 to 0, 0.9s power2.out) while a small elastic settle runs on the disc, and let the ticks draw out and run off the end with drawSVG '0% 100%' then '100% 100%' on a 0.02s stagger. Fade in a heading and a one line receipt. Keep strokes at opacity 0 until they start, since round caps draw a dot at zero length. Add role="status" on the text so assistive tech announces it, wrap in gsap.context and revert on unmount, and skip the tweens under prefers-reduced-motion.

prompt: Build an orbiting icons hero graphic with GSAP 3 MotionPathPlugin. Draw a centre mark and two elliptical orbit paths as SVG (author each ellipse as four cubic curves; make the inner one run counter-clockwise by reversing its path data). Put five rounded icon chips (inline Lucide-style icons, stroke 2) in nested groups: the outer group is moved along the path, the inner group handles depth. Register the plugin and for every chip run gsap.to(chip, { motionPath: { path: orbitEl, align: orbitEl, alignOrigin: [0.5, 0.5] }, duration: 18, ease: 'none', repeat: -1 }), giving the outer orbit 18s and the inner 11s, then call tween.progress(phase) with evenly spaced phases so they start spread out. In onUpdate read gsap.getProperty(chip, 'y'), turn it into t between -1 and 1 across the orbit, and set the inner group to scale 1 + 0.2 * t and opacity 0.72 + 0.28 * (t + 1) / 2 so icons on the near side of the ellipse grow and the far side recede. Add a slow expanding halo behind the centre mark. Use gsap.context and revert on unmount; under prefers-reduced-motion park the chips at their phases without the repeat tween.

title: Progress ring with count
sub: Ring fills while the number counts
prompt: Build a progress ring with a counting number using GSAP 3 and DrawSVGPlugin. Draw the track as a circle (stroke-width 12, pale grey-blue) and the progress as a path made of two arcs that start at 12 o'clock and run clockwise ('M cx cy-r A r r 0 1 1 cx cy+r A r r 0 1 1 cx cy-r'), stroke accent, round caps. Add a white knob with an accent ring as the cap, and a ring of 48 tick marks outside. Register DrawSVGPlugin and drive everything from one eased timeline: gsap.fromTo(ringPath, { drawSVG: '0% 0%' }, { drawSVG: '0% 78%', duration: 1.8, ease: 'power3.out' }) next to gsap.fromTo(state, { p: 0 }, { p: 0.78, duration: 1.8, ease: 'power3.out', onUpdate }) where onUpdate rounds the value into the centre text and places the knob at angle -90deg + p * 360deg using cos and sin of the radius. Using the same ease and duration keeps ring, number and knob locked together. Hold, then run the same tweens back to zero with power2.inOut. Give the SVG role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow updated, wrap in gsap.context and revert on unmount, and jump straight to the final value under prefers-reduced-motion.

prompt: Build a step counter whose big digit redraws itself as the next digit using GSAP 3 MorphSVGPlugin. Draw each digit as a single open centre line path in a 60 by 100 box (1: 'M14 34L34 16L34 84', 2: 'M12 36C12 14 56 12 56 36C56 54 18 68 12 84L56 84', 3: 'M12 22C16 10 56 8 56 30C56 46 38 48 28 48C42 48 58 52 58 68C58 92 14 94 8 74'), stroke-width 8.5, round caps and joins, in your accent colour. One path element is reused: register MorphSVGPlugin and step with gsap.to(path, { morphSVG: { shape: nextD, shapeIndex: 'auto' }, duration: 0.9, ease: 'power3.inOut' }). MorphSVG adds points so the shapes line up; if a pair twists, try an explicit shapeIndex number or type: 'linear'. Cycle 1 to 2 to 3 and back to 1, with a 1.1s hold on each, a step label that fades and shifts under the digit and a small indicator that slides between three dots. Show the digit in a rounded white card. Use gsap.context and revert on unmount; under prefers-reduced-motion switch digits with no tween, and expose the current step in an aria-live region.

prompt: Build a connecting-dots network animation with GSAP 3, DrawSVGPlugin and MotionPathPlugin. Lay out a hub node and six satellites in SVG and connect them with eight slightly curved quadratic paths (edges), stroke-width 2.2 in a pale accent, round caps. Register both plugins. In one timeline: pop the nodes with gsap.fromTo(nodes, { scale: 0 }, { scale: 1, ease: 'back.out(2.2)', stagger: 0.08 }), draw each edge with gsap.fromTo(edges, { drawSVG: '0% 0%' }, { drawSVG: '0% 100%', duration: 0.7, ease: 'power2.inOut', stagger: 0.12 }) so the web grows outward from the hub, then send small packet dots along the lines with gsap.to(packet, { motionPath: { path: edgeEl, align: edgeEl, alignOrigin: [0.5, 0.5], start, end }, duration: 0.85, ease: 'power1.inOut' }). Use start 1 and end 0 to send a packet back down the same line. Reuse a pool of packet elements, hiding each between runs. After a few seconds retract the edges with drawSVG '100% 100%' and shrink the nodes. Wrap in gsap.context and revert on unmount; reduce motion by showing the finished graph with static packets.

title: Liquid button
sub: Hover melts the pill into a gooey shape
prompt: Build a liquid hover button with GSAP 3 MorphSVGPlugin. Draw the button outline as an SVG path (a stadium pill sampled at 24 points, collinear on the straights and every 22.5 degrees on the caps, converted to smooth cubic curves) with a white fill and accent stroke, and stack a second path with the same data and a blue gradient fill at fillOpacity 0 on top. Author a second gooey outline by pushing the same 24 points along their outward normals with a few smooth bumps: a bulge at the top right, a drip at the bottom left, slightly wider overall. Same point count and order keeps the morph clean. Register MorphSVGPlugin and build one paused hover timeline: gsap.to([outline, fill], { morphSVG: { shape: gooD, type: 'linear' }, duration: 0.9, ease: 'elastic.out(1, 0.55)' }), fade the gradient fill in, crossfade the label and arrow from dark to white and nudge them 3px right. Play it on pointerenter and focus, reverse it on pointerleave and blur. Keep a real <button> over the SVG for semantics and keyboard use. Wrap in gsap.context and revert on unmount; with prefers-reduced-motion swap the states with a plain colour change and no morph.
